Writing x = floor(x) + frac(x) and using that floor(km+kt)=km+floor(kt), the argument shows floor(kt)=k-1 for every 1<=k<=n because (n-1)/n <= t < 1. latest_nl_proof:
Let x = m + t, where m = floor(x) ∈ Z and t = frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1).
For each k ∈ {1,2,\dots,n}, since km is an integer we have
floor(kx) = floor(km + kt) = km + floor(kt).
Now t < 1 implies kt < k, so floor(kt) ≤ k-1. Also t ≥ (n-1)/n and k ≤ n, hence
kt ≥ k(n-1)/n = k - k/n ≥ k-1,
so floor(kt) ≥ k-1. Therefore floor(kt) = k-1 for every 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
Thus, for every such k,
floor(kx) = km + k - 1,
and in particular floor(nx) = nm + n - 1.
Substituting into the definition of F_n(x),
F_n(x) = floor(nx) - \sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n (km+k-1)/k
= (nm+n-1) - \sum_{k=1}^n \bigl(m + 1 - 1/k\bigr)
= (nm+n-1) - (nm + n - H_n)
= H_n - 1,
where H_n = \sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Hence whenever frac(x) ∈ [(n-1)/n, 1), we have F_n(x) = H_n - 1.
role_in_parent: Show that the upper bound from the discrete comparison is actually attained on the last interval, giving the full maximizing set.
statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1, define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k, and define frac(x) = x - floor(x). If frac(x) lies in the interval [(n-1)/n, 1), then F_n(x) = H_n - 1, where H_n = sum_{k=1}^{n} 1/k.

domain_restrictions: x is a real number so that floor(x) and frac(x) are defined
the hypothesis constrains frac(x) to be at least (n-1)/n and strictly less than 1
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1 and every real x with fractional part frac(x) in the interval [ (n-1) / n, 1 ), we have F_n(x) equals H_n minus 1, where F_n(x) is floor(n times x) minus the sum for k from 1 to n of (floor(k times x) divided by k), and H_n is the sum for k from 1 to n of 1 divided by k.
quantifier_order: for all n in integers with n > 1
for all real x such that frac(x) is in the interval [(n-1)/n, 1)
